mainTopic: Killing someone other than the intended victim: the dispute between the רבנן and רבי שמעון, and their sources in the פסוקים
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about a blow that missed its target. The attacker is פטור unless the blow was strong enough to kill both where he aimed and where it actually landed. רבי שמעון says that even then, if he meant to kill one person and killed another, he is פטור. The גמרא shows that רבי שמעון is arguing on an inference from the first clause of the משנה, and it asks about unclear cases like 'one of them' or mistaken identity. רבי שמעון learns his view from the פסוק 'וארב לו וקם עליו'. The רבנן use that same פסוק to exclude someone who throws a stone into a group, which is needed when a non-Jew is קבוע among nine Jews. Finally, the רבנן bring proof from the fight that hurt a pregnant woman, where 'נפש תחת נפש' means death. רבי שמעון answers, like רבי, that it means money, and רבי's proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Aimed at the heart, hit the loins: exempt
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes a case that began on the previous page. A man aimed at the victim's heart with a blow strong enough to kill there. It landed on the loins, where it was not strong enough to kill. The victim died anyway, and the attacker is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and the blow was strong enough to kill on his heart, but it landed on his loins, and it was not strong enough to kill on his loins, and he died: the attacker is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing a case it started on the previous page. A blow aimed at the heart hit the loins instead, and the attacker is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He really wanted to kill, and his blow would have killed if it hit the heart. But the blow that actually landed was too weak to kill someone on the loins. So we do not blame his blow for the death, and he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: To kill (the blow is strong enough to cause death)
His loins / lower back, a less sensitive area
His heart (the chest over the heart), a sensitive area

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence. The beginning, 'he intended to strike him on his heart', is on the previous page.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה בָּהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית עַל לִבּוֹ,
phrases.english: and it [the blow] had enough force to kill on his heart,
but it went and landed on his loins,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיָה בָּהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית עַל מׇתְנָיו,
phrases.english: and it did not have enough force to kill on his loins,
and he died: [the attacker is] exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָיָה בָּהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית עַל לִבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's case from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the blow was not deadly where it actually landed, the attacker is פטור even though the victim died.

steps.title: Aimed at an adult or a minor, hit the other: two exempt cases
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives two more cases where the attacker is פטור. In each one, the blow was not deadly for one of the two people: the one he aimed at, or the one it actually hit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he meant to hit an adult, and the blow was not strong enough to kill an adult, but it hit a minor and was strong enough to kill a minor, and the minor died: exempt. If he meant to hit a minor, and it was strong enough to kill a minor, but it hit an adult and was not strong enough to kill an adult, and the adult died anyway: exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two cases where the blow hit a different person than the one aimed at, and in both the attacker is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, the blow was deadly for the minor it hit, but he had aimed a blow too weak to kill the adult he wanted to kill. So he never planned a deadly blow. In the second case, he planned a deadly blow, but it was too weak to kill the adult it hit. Either way, the blow was not deadly on both sides, so he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor / child (weaker, easier to kill)

phrases.english: If he intended to strike the adult,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיָה בָּהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית הַגָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: and it did not have enough force to kill the adult,
and it went and landed on the minor,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה בָּהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית אֶת הַקָּטָן,
phrases.english: and it had enough force to kill the minor,
and he died: [the attacker is] exempt.
If he intended to strike the minor,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה בָּהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית אֶת הַקָּטָן,
phrases.english: and it had enough force to kill the minor,
and it went and landed on the adult,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיָה בָּהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית אֶת הַגָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: and it did not have enough force to kill the adult,
and he died: [the attacker is] exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִתְכַּוֵּון לְהַכּוֹת אֶת הַגָּדוֹל, וְלֹא הָיָה בָּהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית הַגָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same rule as Step 1 to a blow that hits a different person instead of a different spot.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the blow was not deadly both for the one he aimed at and for the one it hit, the attacker is פטור.

steps.title: Blow deadly in both places: liable
steps.stepSummary: The משנה now gives the opposite cases. When the blow was deadly where he aimed and also deadly where it landed, the attacker is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he meant to hit him on the loins, and the blow was strong enough to kill on the loins, but it landed on his heart and he died: liable. If he meant to hit an adult, and it was strong enough to kill an adult, but it hit a minor and he died: liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה switches to cases where the attacker is liable. The blow was strong enough to kill even where he aimed, so it was surely deadly where it landed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blow that can kill on the loins can surely kill on the heart. A blow that can kill an adult can surely kill a child. So he planned a deadly blow, and the blow that landed was also deadly. That is why the תנא קמא holds him חייב, even though it hit a different spot or a different person.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the first opinion in the משנה, he is חייב only if the blow was deadly both where he aimed and where it actually landed.

phrases.english: But if he intended to strike [him] on his loins,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה בָּהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית עַל מׇתְנָיו,
phrases.english: and it had enough force to kill on his loins,
and it went and landed on his heart,
and he died: [the attacker is] liable.
If he intended to strike the adult,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה בָּהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית אֶת הַגָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: and it had enough force to kill the adult,
and it went and landed on the minor,
and he died: [the attacker is] liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The flip side of Steps 1 and 2. When the blow is deadly on both sides, he is liable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blow deadly both at the target and at the actual landing spot or person makes the attacker חייב.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: killing the wrong person is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון argues. Even if he meant to kill one person and killed another, he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: even if he intended to kill this one and killed that one, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה. He says that killing someone other than the intended victim makes the attacker exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, it is not enough that the blow was deadly. The killing must match the plan: the person he meant to kill must be the person who died. If the victim was switched, there is no death penalty.

keyTerms.term: לַהֲרוֹג אֶת זֶה וְהָרַג אֶת זֶה
keyTerms.meaning: To kill this one, and he killed that one (a switched victim)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's question about exactly which case of the משנה רבי שמעון is arguing on.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Even if he intended to kill this one
and he killed that one: [he is] exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ נִתְכַּוֵּון לַהֲרוֹג אֶת זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comes right after the liable rulings. Which ruling it actually argues with is the question the גמרא takes up in Steps 5-7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, one who killed a different person than the one he intended is פטור.

steps.title: Which case is רבי שמעון arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking which part of the משנה רבי שמעון is disagreeing with.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי שמעון — on which part [of the משנה] is he arguing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion with a question: which ruling in the משנה is רבי שמעון arguing against? This opens the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has several cases, and רבי שמעון's words could be aimed at more than one of them. The גמרא wants to pin down exactly where the argument is.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
On which one? (which part is being discussed)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Shimon — on which [part of the Mishnah is he arguing]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of רבי שמעון's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ruling in the משנה רבי שמעון is disputing.

steps.title: He can't mean only the last case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי שמעון is arguing about the last case (aimed at an adult, killed a minor). It rejects this from the wording: if so, the משנה should simply have said 'רבי שמעון פוטר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he is arguing on the last case, it should have said 'רבי שמעון exempts'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first answer, that רבי שמעון is arguing on the last case. It attacks this answer from the way the משנה is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי שמעון only disagreed with the last case, the משנה could just say 'רבי שמעון פוטר'. Instead it gives a long statement starting with 'אפילו', 'even'. That suggests he is adding something new, beyond the last case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion to test)
The last part of a משנה

phrases.english: If you say [he argues] on the last clause,
it should have said, "Rabbi Shimon exempts"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא אַסֵּיפָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן פּוֹטֵר מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question in Step 5 and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי שמעון is arguing only on the last case of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The long phrasing with 'אפילו' does not fit a simple disagreement on the last case. For that, 'רבי שמעון פוטר' would have been enough.

steps.title: רבי שמעון argues on the first clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון disagrees with an inference from the first clause: aiming at one person and killing a different person makes him חייב. רבי שמעון says he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he is arguing on the first part of the משנה. It says that if someone meant to kill an animal and killed a person, or meant to kill a non-Jew and killed a Jew, or meant to kill a baby that could not survive and killed a person who could live, he is פטור. That means if he meant to kill this person and killed that person, he is חייב. On that, רבי שמעון says: even if he meant to kill this person and killed that one, he is פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: The last step rejected the idea that רבי שמעון argues on the final case. Now the גמרא says he argues on the first clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause gives cases where the person he aimed at was not someone you can be killed for killing. From this we can infer that if both people are real people (this one and that one), he is חייב. רבי שמעון's words 'even if he meant this one and killed that one' fit perfectly as an argument against that inference.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting the earlier suggestion and giving a new one)
The first clause of the משנה

phrases.english: Rather, he argues on the first clause:
If he intended to kill the animal
and he killed the person,
or a non-Jew, and he killed a Jew,

phrases.aramaic: לַנְּפָלִים וְהָרַג אֶת בֶּן קַיָּימָא – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: or non-viable babies, and he killed a viable person: he is exempt.
This implies that if he intended to kill this one
and killed that one, he is liable.
phrases.notes: The משנה never says this line out loud. The גמרא is reading it out of the first clause.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Even if he intended to kill this one
and killed that one, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected placement from step 6 with a new one
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון argues on the implied ruling of the first clause: aiming at one person and killing another makes him חייב.

steps.title: The obvious case of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: If ראובן and שמעון stand there and he says clearly that he means ראובן and not שמעון, that is clearly the case they argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious: if ראובן and שמעון are standing there and he says, 'I mean to kill ראובן, not שמעון,' that is exactly what they argue about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the clear case of the argument. It is setting up the questions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here his intent was clear and specific, and he hit the other person. Everyone agrees this is the case where the רבנן say חייב and רבי שמעון says פטור. The unclear cases come in the next step.

phrases.english: It is obvious!
If Reuven and Shimon are standing,
and he said: 'I intend to kill Reuven,
I do not intend to kill Shimon,'
this is their dispute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the clear case of the dispute just placed in step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clear intent for Reuven, killing Shimon, is the case the רבנן and רבי שמעון argue about.

steps.title: Unclear cases: 'one of them' or mistaken identity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks two questions: what if he said he means one of them, without picking which? And what if he thought the person was ראובן, but it turned out to be שמעון?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said, 'I mean one of them,' what is the law? Or, if he thought it was ראובן and it turned out to be שמעון, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about two harder cases that are less clear than the obvious one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case he wanted to kill whichever one he hit, so maybe he really did intend the victim. In the second case he aimed at the very person standing in front of him and was only wrong about the name. The question is whether רבי שמעון still says פטור in these cases.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought it was this, and it turned out to be that

phrases.english: If he said: 'For one of them,' what is the law?
Or alternatively, if he thought it was Reuven
and it turned out to be Shimon, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the obvious case to two unclear ones
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי שמעון also say פטור when he meant 'one of them', or when he was mistaken about the victim's identity?

steps.title: A ברייתא: he must intend a specific person
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון: he is not חייב until he says 'I mean so-and-so.' This suggests both unclear cases are פטור according to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says, he is not חייב until he says, 'I mean to kill so-and-so.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the questions of the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון requires intent toward one specific, named person, and that this same person is the one killed. 'One of them' does not name anyone. Thinking it was ראובן means his intent was for ראובן, not for שמעון who was killed. So in both cases he would not be חייב.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught:
Rabbi Shimon says,
not until he says: 'I intend to kill so-and-so.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the questions of step 9 with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון's view in the unclear cases
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'עד שיאמר לפלוני אני מתכוון'
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, a killer is חייב only if he intended a specific person and killed that very person.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי שמעון gets his view from.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי שמעון's rule. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we have only heard what רבי שמעון holds. Now the גמרא wants to know which פסוק it comes from.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from what רבי שמעון holds to why he holds it
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי שמעון's rule

steps.title: The פסוק: 'he lies in wait for him'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'he lies in wait for him and rises up against him', so he is only חייב if he meant to kill that very person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'He lies in wait for him and rises up against him.' This teaches that he is not חייב until he intends to kill him, the victim himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the פסוק behind רבי שמעון's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'for him' and 'against him' point at the actual victim. רבי שמעון reads them to mean the killer must have planned to kill that same person. If he aimed at someone else, he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: And he lies in wait for him

phrases.english: The verse says:
'And he lies in wait for him and rises up against him,'
not until he intends to kill him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא וְאָרַב לוֹ וְקָם עָלָיו
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'וארב לו וקם עליו': he must intend the actual victim.

steps.title: The רבנן use the פסוק for throwing a stone into a group
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן, who disagree with רבי שמעון, use the same פסוק to exclude someone who throws a stone into a group of people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they learn from this פסוק? The school of רבי ינאי said: it comes to exclude someone who throws a stone into a group.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן do with this פסוק and answers in the name of the school of רבי ינאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן agree that the killer must intend some person. They only use 'for him' to exclude a case where he aimed at no one in particular, like throwing a stone into a crowd. They do not learn from it that he must kill the exact person he aimed at.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who disagree with רבי שמעון

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: This is a short question: what do the רבנן learn from this same פסוק?

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai say:
To exclude one who throws a stone into a group.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the other side reads the same פסוק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן use the פסוק to exclude one who throws a stone into a group.

steps.title: Why is a פסוק needed for the stone case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the group case looks like. If most are non-Jews, we would already go after the majority. If it is half and half, a doubt in a life-and-death case is judged leniently. Either way, no פסוק seems needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If there are nine non-Jews and one Jew among them, we already know he is פטור because most of them are non-Jews. And if it is half and half, a doubt in a case of life and death is judged leniently.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for the רבנן's derivation from the פסוק. It is setting up an answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a majority of non-Jews, we assume the stone was thrown toward a non-Jew, so he is פטור without a פסוק. In a half-and-half group there is a doubt, and in a case of life and death we never punish on a doubt. So the גמרא asks which case the פסוק could be needed for.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
A doubt in a life-and-death case is judged leniently

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say that there are nine non-Jews
and one Jew among them,
derive it from the fact that most of them are non-Jews.
Or if it is half and half,
a doubt in a capital case is ruled leniently.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא דְּאִיכָּא תִּשְׁעָה גּוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the derivation given in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's use of the פסוק to exclude throwing a stone into a group
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every way of setting up the case is already פטור from other rules (majority, or leniency in doubt), so the פסוק seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The group case: nine Jews and one non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is needed for a group of nine Jews and one non-Jew. Since the non-Jew is קבוע (fixed in place), the case counts as half and half.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the פסוק is needed for a case of nine Jews with one non-Jew among them. The non-Jew is fixed in place, and anything fixed is treated like half and half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 14 by describing a group case where the פסוק really is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we follow the majority, so nine Jews would make him חייב. But the non-Jew is fixed in the group, and the rule of קבוע says a fixed item counts as half and half. So we do not follow the majority, and the פסוק tells us he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for... (introduces a narrower case)
Like half and half (an even doubt)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'nine Jews' means we follow the majority here. Because the non-Jew is קבוע, the majority rule does not apply.

phrases.english: No, it is needed only
where there are nine Jews
and one non-Jew among them
so it is a case of a non-Jew who is fixed in place
phrases.notes: He is standing right there in the group. He is not someone who wandered away from it.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל קָבוּעַ כְּמֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: and anything fixed is treated like half and half.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאִיכָּא תִּשְׁעָה יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹי אֶחָד בֵּינֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 14 by finding a case that is neither a plain majority nor an ordinary half-and-half doubt.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Majority Jews means we follow the majority, so no פסוק would be needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the non-Jew is קבוע, the majority is ignored. The פסוק is needed to teach that he is פטור.

steps.title: The רבנן have a source, so what does רבי שמעון do with 'a life for a life'?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן prove from the fighting men and the pregnant woman that intending to kill one person and killing another makes you חייב. The גמרא asks how רבי שמעון explains that פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the רבנן, who say that someone who meant to kill one person and killed another is חייב. The פסוק says 'If men fight and hurt a pregnant woman', and רבי אלעזר says the fight was a deadly one, because it says 'if there is a tragedy, give a life for a life.' But רבי שמעון holds he is פטור, so what does he do with 'a life for a life'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the רבנן have a clear פסוק for their view. It then challenges רבי שמעון to explain that same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר says the men were trying to kill each other. One of them killed the woman instead, and the פסוק says 'a life for a life', which means death. That fits the רבנן perfectly. רבי שמעון says such a killer is פטור, so the phrase 'נפש תחת נפש' seems to go against him.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (for one side)... sets up a contrast

keyTerms.term: נִתְכַּוֵּון לַהֲרוֹג אֶת זֶה וְהָרַג אֶת זֶה
keyTerms.meaning: He meant to kill one person and killed another
A fight where each wants to kill the other
What does he do with it? (how does he explain it)

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the Rabbis, who say:
if one intended to kill this person
and he killed that person, he is liable
as it is written: "If men struggle
and they hurt a pregnant woman."
And Rabbi Elazar says:
the verse is speaking about a deadly fight
as it is written: "If there shall be a tragedy
then you shall give a life for a life."
But according to Rabbi Shimon
this "then you shall give a life for a life"
what does he do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the group case and challenges רבי שמעון's basic view from a different פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's view that someone who meant to kill one person and killed another is פטור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The pregnant-woman פסוק, as רבי אלעזר reads it, gives the death penalty to someone who killed a person he did not mean to kill.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: 'a life for a life' means money
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון reads 'נפש תחת נפש' as paying money, following רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He reads it as money, like רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבי שמעון the phrase means paying money, not the death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'a life for a life' means money, the פסוק no longer proves that the killer is put to death. So רבי שמעון's view of פטור from death stays standing. The גמרא backs this reading by tying it to רבי.

phrases.english: Monetary restitution.
And this is in accordance with Rabbi,

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It means paying money, as רבי teaches.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי שמעון, 'נפש תחת נפש' means paying money, as רבי teaches. So the פסוק does not prove a death penalty for killing someone other than the intended victim.

steps.title: רבי's ברייתא: 'a life for a life' means money
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי saying 'נפש תחת נפש' means money. He proves it by comparing the word 'giving' here with 'giving' in another פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: רבי says 'give a life for a life' means money. You say money, but maybe it means an actual life? 'Giving' is said below, and it is said...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that is the source for רבי's reading. It starts to prove 'money' from the word 'giving', and the proof continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first asks whether the phrase might mean taking an actual life. To answer, it compares the word 'ונתתה' (giving) in our פסוק with the same word in a nearby פסוק. The comparison is only partly quoted here.

phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi says
"Then you shall give a life for a life" means money.
Do you say it means money
or does it mean only an actual life?
Giving is stated below
and giving is stated

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא source for the 'money' reading mentioned in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That 'נפש תחת נפש' means money, not death
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי that compares the word 'giving' in two פסוקים (the comparison continues on the next amud)
